pages.title: ORSA Continuity Protocol
pages.text: $(bold)Continuity protocol: active.$()$(br2)Emergency EVA supplies ten minutes of reserve oxygen and thermal control following equipment loss in late Phase 6. Missing suit components are issued automatically upon return.$(br2)Recover a serviceable rig or return to recorded shelter. This equipment is disposable. Its service clock is shared across all issued pieces.

pages.title: Recorded Shelter
pages.text: Setting your respawn point at a bed or charged anchor records a shelter automatically.$(br2)The position record is degraded. Follow the approximate bearing, then search within 32 blocks of the estimated fix. The estimate remains consistent across replacement issues.$(br2)$(italic)Recorded locations do not constitute confirmation of habitable conditions.$()

pages.title: Last Telemetry
pages.text: The suit archives the location of equipment loss. Use $(k:key.frozendawn.continuity_target) to switch between LAST TELEMETRY and LAST SHELTER.$(br2)Telemetry records a position, not the continued presence of your equipment. Subsequent empty-handed emergency losses preserve the original destination.$(br2)Equipment from the qualifying loss has fifteen minutes of lifetime while its area is ticking. Fire, lava and other hazards still apply.

pages.title: Service Limits
pages.text: Inventory service bars track the same reserve as the HUD. Impacts still injure the wearer, but do not shorten emergency service. Progressive seal deterioration appears at the visor edges.$(br2)At zero, oxygen, thermal control, navigation and emergency armor protection end. Spent pieces remain until replaced.$(br2)Removing every issued piece pauses service and removes its life support. Repair, cartridges and replacement issues cannot refresh old equipment.
